visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young woman with long dark hair, wearing a grey long-sleeved top and light-colored pants, stands in a brightly lit indoor studio. She points towards a tripod with a smartphone mounted on it, her facial expression animated and her mouth open as she speaks. The background features a wooden cabinet and white curtains. (2) The scene shifts to a close-up of a smartphone on a tripod. In the camera's viewfinder, a woman is seen sitting on a yellow sofa against a white brick wall. She gestures with her hand, and the phone screen indicates a photo is being captured. (3) A close-up view shows a smartphone lying on a wooden table, covered with clear plastic wrap. A pair of hands with black nail polish uses an orange marker to draw a circular mark on the plastic wrap, precisely over the position of the camera's shutter button. (4) A screen recording sequence displays the iPhone settings menu. It navigates through 'Accessibility', 'Voice Control', and 'Customize Commands' to create a new voice command. The text entry '幫我拍照' is shown being typed into the command field before selecting 'Run Custom Gesture'. (5) The main character returns to the frame holding the smartphone. She speaks the voice command, and the phone captures a photo. She smiles broadly at the camera and gives a thumbs-up gesture, expressing success and satisfaction with the newly set-up feature in the studio. (6) A different young woman with shorter hair, wearing a heavy black coat with a fur collar, enters a modern office hallway. She looks surprised and poses with a white smartphone, showing an exaggerated facial expression while the red 'aotter' logo is visible on the wall behind her.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: This video is a instructional guide teaching iPhone users how to utilize the 'Voice Control' accessibility feature to take photos hands-free. It uses a clever physical hack involving plastic wrap and a marker to map the shutter button's location, making it easier for users to take group shots or selfies without relying on timers.
